hypothesis: Adding a masked cosine-similarity penalty between predicted and target wind vectors constrains the forecast head in polar direction, reducing the systematic wind_x overprediction and the wind_x-dominated T+8 errors that plain Cartesian MSE leaves under-constrained.
evidence_anchor: All weakest forecast RMSE slices are wind_x at T+8 (ZBAA 0.0578, ZSSS 0.0575, ZSPD 0.0560) and ZSSS T+1 wind_x shows overprediction >1; normalized wind components are Cartesian, so MSE alone does not directly penalize correlated vector-direction error.
expected_effect: paired fc_scratch RMSE improves by 0.0005 to 0.002 relative to parent; T+8 wind_x slices improve by 0.001 to 0.003; ZSSS T+1 wind_x overprediction is reduced.
falsification: If paired fc_scratch RMSE improvement is < 0.0005, or if mean RMSE over ZBAA/ZSSS T+8 wind_x slices does not improve relative to parent, the trial is refuted.
patch_plan: In forecast_loss, compute the base masked MSE as before. Then split prediction and target along dim=3 into wind_x and wind_y, compute vector cosine similarity per active element with epsilon=1e-6, and add lambda * masked_mean(1 - cosine_similarity) with lambda=0.2. Return the sum of base MSE and the angular penalty.
non_expressibility: Closest templates O1-horizon-weighted-mse and O2-event-weighted-loss reweight squared-error terms along different axes but cannot express a polar directional penalty that couples wind_x and wind_y through cosine similarity. This functional form is outside all active template parameter spaces.
